title: The Open Proclamation
year: c. 613 CE — the fourth year of prophethood
teaser: Four men sat down to find one word for the Qur'an. They tried soothsayer, madman, poet — and failed.

layers.title: The Order to Speak
layers.subtitle: Three years of whispering come to an end
layers.content:
For three years the call had travelled by word of mouth. A man heard it in private, believed in private, and prayed where no one could see him. Al-Mubarakpuri describes what those years produced: a small body of believers bound by brotherhood, with one purpose held in common. Then the instruction changed.

The verse that changed it was «وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ» — 'And warn your tribe of near kindred.' (26:214) It was the first verse revealed on this matter. Where it sits is part of its meaning. Surah ash-Shu'ara walks through Musa's long confrontation with Pharaoh, then names nation after nation that called its messenger a liar: the people of Nuh, Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut, the companions of the wood. The command to speak arrived wrapped in the record of what happens to those who refuse to hear.

A second verse settled the manner of it: «فَاصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ» — 'Therefore proclaim openly that which you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists.' (15:94)

Makkah was a city governed by descent. A man's safety came from his clan, and a clan's standing came from its share in the sanctuary and the trade the pilgrims brought. In such a city, a message that called the idols worthless was not a private opinion. It touched the income of every household and the memory of every dead father. The Prophet ﷺ was now instructed to say it in public, by name, from a hillside where the whole valley could see him standing.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 26:214 — 'And warn your tribe of near kindred'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Warning at the Gathering
layers.subtitle: He called them, then he named his own daughter
layers.content:
Muslim records, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, what the Prophet ﷺ did when the verse came down. He called the people of Quraysh. They gathered. He gave them a general warning, then began naming them in narrowing circles: 'O Quraysh, rescue yourselves from the Fire. O people of Bani Ka'b, rescue yourselves from the Fire.' Then he reached inside his own house: 'O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, rescue yourself from the Fire — for I have no power to protect you from Allah in anything, except that I would keep the ties of kinship with you.'

In a city where blood was the highest court, no sentence could have unsettled them more. He was telling his own relatives that being related to him bought them nothing.

At the gathering on as-Safa his uncle Abu Lahab answered him: perish you, is it for this that you called us together. The reply came down as a whole surah: «تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ» — 'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he.' (111:1) His wife Umm Jamil, the sister of Abu Sufyan, is named in the same three lines as the one who carries the firewood.

After this nothing was concealed. He recited the Qur'an at the assemblies of the idolaters. He prayed aloud in the courtyard of the Ka'bah in daylight while they watched. He said openly that the stones could neither act nor intercede. People kept entering Islam, one after another, and each new convert found himself set against his own family.

Abu Lahab did not confine himself to speeches. When the pilgrim fairs opened at Ukaz, Majannah and Dhul-Majaz, he followed the Prophet ﷺ from camp to camp calling out ahead of him: do not listen to this man, he is a liar, he has left his religion.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 111:1 — 'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he'
layers.hadith_ref: The warning to Quraysh and to Fatimah — Sahih Muslim, narrated by Abu Hurairah; also Sahih al-Bukhari
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Committee and the Purse
layers.subtitle: First they tried to name him, then to buy him
layers.content:
The proclamation was a few months old when Quraysh saw their real difficulty. The pilgrimage season was approaching. Arab delegations would arrive from every direction, and this man would speak to all of them. They went to al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and asked him for one accusation they could all repeat.

Ibn Hisham preserves the discussion. Call him a soothsayer — rejected, his speech did not fall into a soothsayer's rhythm. Call him possessed by jinn — rejected, none of the signs were there to point at. A poet, then — rejected, his words lay outside poetry altogether. A worker of witchcraft — al-Walid hesitated again, saying the man had never been seen blowing on knots, and admitting that his speech was sweet in its entirety, root and branch. What they finally agreed on was that his sorcery was his eloquence: an art strong enough to split a son from his father, a man from his brother, a wife from her husband, a man from his clan. That was the formula, and they carried it to the pilgrims.

Later came the other approach. Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, one of their chiefs, went to the Prophet ﷺ with an offer, and the sirah places this after two conversions had already shifted the balance in Makkah. If you want wealth, we will gather for you more than any man of Quraysh owns. If you want rank, we will make you our chief. If you want kingship, we will hand it to you. If a spirit has taken hold of you, we will pay physicians to cure you.

The Prophet ﷺ asked whether he had finished. Then he recited Surah Fussilat to him and prostrated at its place of prostration, and said: Abul-Walid, you have heard my reply.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 41:1-5 — the surah recited in answer to Utbah's offer
layers.source: Ibn Hisham 1/271 and 1/293-294, in Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Revelation
layers.subtitle: Every label they invented was written down
layers.content:
Al-Walid's committee received sixteen verses of its own. They describe a man thinking, weighing, frowning, turning away in pride, and arriving at his verdict: «إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ» — 'This is nothing but magic from that of old; this is nothing but the word of a human being.' (74:18-25)

The Qur'an did not argue with the charge. It recorded how the charge was manufactured — proposed, tested, discarded, replaced — and left the reader to notice that a verdict reached by elimination is not a verdict about anything.

Abu Lahab's outburst became Surah al-Masad: his hands, his wealth, his wife who carries firewood. Of all the men in Makkah who opposed the message, the one named in the Book is the one closest by blood.

The answer to Utbah was Surah Fussilat: «حم • تَنزِيلٌ مِّنَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ» — 'Ha-Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are set out in detail, a Qur'an in Arabic for people who know. Giving glad tidings and warning — but most of them turn away, so they do not listen. And they say: our hearts are covered from that to which you invite us.' (41:1-5) The verses did not respond to the offer. They described the man making it: someone being spoken to, who has decided in advance not to hear.

The nicknames were settled the same way. 'You are a madman' (15:6). 'A sorcerer, a liar' (38:4). 'Verily he is a madman' (68:51). Each is quoted in the Qur'an as the speech of the accusers — preserved, not erased, so that the accusation would be recited for as long as the Book was recited.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 74:18-25 — the verses revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: What It Left Behind
layers.subtitle: The enemies gave the best testimony
layers.content:
Going public cost the Muslims their safety. It bought three things.

It made the message a public fact. After as-Safa no one in Makkah could say he had not heard. The argument was no longer about whether Muhammad ﷺ was saying something. It was about whether it was true.

It cut belief loose from lineage. When he told his own daughter that being his daughter would not shield her from the Fire, he spent the only currency Arabia fully understood. Every conversion after that was a person choosing against his own clan — which is why the persecution that followed fell heaviest on those who had no clan behind them.

And it produced, from the mouths of enemies, the best testimony about the Qur'an that survives. Al-Walid could not find a category for it and settled on calling its beauty a spell. Utbah came to buy silence and went back to his people saying he had never heard words like these, that they were not poetry, not witchcraft, not soothsaying, and that if the man gained power over the Arabs they would share in his kingship. Al-Mubarakpuri records the reply of the assembly: they laughed and said Muhammad had bewitched him too.

Here is the thing to carry. The strongest objection Quraysh ever raised against the Qur'an was that it worked. They did not argue that it was false. They argued that it was dangerous — that it took sons from fathers and wives from husbands. Anyone today who keeps the Book at a careful distance might ask which of those two reasons he is actually using.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 6:33 — 'We know indeed the grief which their words cause you'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

quiz.prompt: Which verse does al-Mubarakpuri identify as the first revealed commanding the Prophet ﷺ to preach openly?

options.text: 'Arise and warn' (74:2)
'And warn your tribe of near kindred' (26:214)
'Convey what has been revealed to you' (5:67)
'Say: I am only a warner' (38:65)

quiz.scholar_reflection: It sits inside Surah ash-Shu'ara, a chapter about Musa against Pharaoh and about nations that called their messengers liars. The command to speak came with the history of refusal attached to it.

quiz.prompt: In the narration of Abu Hurairah, whom did the Prophet ﷺ name last as he warned Quraysh group by group?

options.text: Abu Talib, his uncle and protector
Khadijah, his wife
Fatimah, his own daughter
The chiefs of Bani Makhzum

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim, narrated by Abu Hurairah; also Sahih al-Bukhari
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'Rescue yourself from the Fire, for I have no power to protect you from Allah in anything.' He began with a whole tribe and ended inside his own household.

quiz.prompt: Whom did Quraysh consult to agree on a single accusation to repeat to the arriving pilgrims?

options.text: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham
al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah
Umayyah ibn Khalaf
an-Nadr ibn al-Harith

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/271 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: They needed one formula because contradicting each other in front of the delegations would have been worse than saying nothing.

quiz.prompt: What accusation did al-Walid's council finally settle on, after rejecting soothsayer, madman and poet?

options.text: That he had copied the scriptures of the Jews and Christians
That he was a foreign agent working for Abyssinia
That his eloquence was itself a sorcery, splitting a man from his family and clan
That he sought only wealth and rank

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/271 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: Al-Walid admitted the speech was sweet root and branch, then called that sweetness magic. Sixteen verses of Surah al-Muddaththir record how he arrived at it.

quiz.prompt: What did Utbah ibn Rabi'ah offer the Prophet ﷺ in exchange for silence?

options.text: Safe passage out of Makkah for him and his followers
Wealth, chieftaincy, kingship, or physicians if a spirit had taken hold of him
A permanent seat on the council of Quraysh
Custody of the keys of the Ka'bah

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/293-294 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: The reply was not a counter-offer. It was Surah Fussilat recited to the end of its prostration, and then: Abul-Walid, you have heard my reply.

quiz.prompt: He warned Quraysh in narrowing circles and finished with his own daughter, telling her that kinship with him would not protect her from Allah. What do you take from a man dismantling his own strongest social advantage?

options.text: It proved the message was not a family project dressed up as revelation
It was costly in exactly the way a truthful warning has to be
It set the terms early: accountability is individual, and no relation cancels it
It was the hardest thing he could have said, which is why he said it

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim, narrated by Abu Hurairah
quiz.scholar_reflection: He did not exempt Fatimah. Every claim of privileged access made since then runs into this sentence.

quiz.prompt: Four men wanted the Qur'an dismissed. They tried soothsayer, madman, poet and sorcerer, and rejected each one as not fitting. What does their failure to find a label tell you?

options.text: The Qur'an did not belong to any category of Arabic speech they knew
They were not seeking the truth about it, only a usable word against it
Their final answer conceded the point — they called its beauty a kind of magic
Honest experts of the language failed to place it, and that itself is evidence

quiz.scholar_reflection: These were the finest critics of Arabic alive. Their considered verdict was that it did not sound like anything a human produces — so they called it a spell.

quiz.prompt: Utbah offered wealth, rank, kingship, and medical treatment — everything a man of that world could want — for silence. What stands out to you about being offered everything to stop?

options.text: They assumed he wanted what they wanted, because they could not imagine another motive
The offer was itself an admission that they could not answer the message
Silence was worth more to them than any of the things they were offering
Recitation as an answer refused the whole frame of the negotiation

quiz.slider_label: The price they put on silence
quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/293-294 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: Utbah went back with a changed face. He told his people the words were not poetry, not witchcraft, not soothsaying. They said he had been bewitched too.

quiz.prompt: The man who shouted him down at as-Safa, followed him between the pilgrim camps to call him a liar, and had a surah revealed against him was his own uncle. How do you sit with opposition that comes from inside the family?

options.text: It is the sharpest kind, because it cannot be dismissed as ignorance of who you are
Nearness of blood gives no advantage in faith, and Abu Lahab is the proof
Abu Talib and Abu Lahab were both uncles — the same relation produced opposite responses
It is a warning against assuming proximity to guidance transmits it

quiz.scholar_reflection: He lived next door. He knew the man's character better than any pilgrim in Ukaz. He chose the position he chose anyway.

quiz.prompt: After the command came, he prayed aloud in the courtyard of the Ka'bah in daylight while the leaders of Quraysh watched. What does that choice ask of a person who would rather practise quietly?

options.text: Some things stop being true in practice if they are only ever done in private
Concealment had been permitted for three years — so visibility is a stage, not a constant duty
He bore the exposure himself before asking anyone else to bear it
The point was not defiance but refusing to treat the truth as embarrassing

quiz.scholar_reflection: Note the order. Three years hidden, then the command, then the courtyard. Timing was part of the instruction, not a lapse in courage.
